bounds.domain: One Android deployment, one predecessor and successor, two same-generation claim contenders (the second may hold a stale predecessor read), one durable encrypted request/receipt slot, one newer credential action, one partial selected-slot publication, two restarts and six total exact ACK requests. Request claims cannot be stolen. A dispatched pre-secret claim survives uncertain replies; a full successor receipt preserves secret, proof and stable proposed identity across restart.
bounds.assumptions: Slot CAS and authoritative durable readback are atomic under the original durable credential generation. A newer user action fences old recovery. Server ACK200 with the exact credential ID activates the successor and erases its recoverable ciphertext; exact committed ACK replay remains available after the original deadline. PKCE, secrets, IDs, generation and JSON validation are opaque identities exercised by the JVM conformance fixtures. A request dispatch rechecks the selected predecessor after its claim.
bounds.limitations: This is a finite safety projection, not a liveness or device proof. Time is represented by a deadline event; request expiry warnings, actual backoff durations and daily preference persistence are covered by the JVM fixtures. The request-only recovery outcome abstracts the recent deferred/24-hour sign-in-required distinction, and never frees the claim. Revocation delivery is modeled as immediate success with the successor header; durable retry timing and optional best-effort host notification are checked in JVM fixtures. Permanent storage/network failure, cryptography, Android scheduling, arbitrary processes and Cloud routes themselves remain separate. Partial publication represents a host metadata/token write gap; recovery can repair it only with the original generation and a confirmed receipt.
